"Ensures automated information security and privacy capabilities are integrated and deployed as required..." (Excerpt 4)
gaps: No explicit policy requirement to deploy, configure, or use antivirus/anti-malware solutions.
No mention of keeping virus/malware definitions up to date.
No requirement for conducting regular scans for malware.
No assignment of accountability or metrics for antivirus effectiveness.
recommendations: Explicitly require the deployment and configuration of antivirus and anti-malware technologies on all assets.
Mandate automatic updating of antivirus/anti-malware definitions and specify minimum update frequency.
Require regular (at least weekly) malware scans on all assets.
Define responsibilities and accountability for maintaining and monitoring antivirus solutions.
Integrate metrics and reporting on antivirus/anti-malware status and effectiveness into the continuous monitoring program.

control_results.score_rationale: The policy defines roles, responsibilities, and core processes for vulnerability identification, tracking, and remediation, including requirements for patching and documenting weaknesses. However, there is no explicit mention of program-level oversight, defined metrics, continuous improvement, or integration with risk management beyond basic compliance.
evidence: Ensures continuous monitoring of the information system’s security is performed and validates the information system against the System Security Plan (SSP) while managing and controlling any information system updates;
Ensures that security patches for all assigned information systems are installed within the timeframe identified by ED policy;
Ensuring that all security related documentation for their systems are updated according to applicable guidance and standards;
Ensures, in coordination with CORs and acquisition personnel, that cybersecurity is addressed in all IT-related procurements and contracts through appropriate language in requirements documents;

Assists their applicable System Owner in capturing all system weaknesses, policy and standard deviations in the POA&M and entering them into the Department’s selected central cybersecurity repository (currently CSAM);
Ensures that system weaknesses are captured in the Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M) and are entered into ED’s selected Central Cybersecurity Repository (currently CSAM);
gaps: No explicit reference to program-level oversight for the vulnerability management program as a whole.
Lacks specific mention of metrics or reporting to measure the effectiveness of vulnerability management.
Does not address continuous improvement or feedback to optimize vulnerability management processes.
No clear integration of vulnerability management findings with overall risk management beyond basic compliance.
Does not specify methods or tools for vulnerability scanning or assessment.
recommendations: Establish program-level oversight with a designated owner for the vulnerability management function.
Define and implement metrics to measure the timeliness and effectiveness of vulnerability identification and remediation.
Incorporate regular reviews and updates of the vulnerability management process for continuous improvement.
Integrate vulnerability management outcomes with enterprise risk management processes to prioritize remediation activities based on risk.
Specify standardized tools and procedures for vulnerability scanning, assessment, and tracking.

control_results.score_rationale: The policy formally assigns roles and responsibilities for vulnerability remediation and patching, outlines adherence to defined timelines, and references compliance with ED policy and external directives. However, it lacks explicit definition of SLAs, measurable metrics, and details on risk-based prioritization of vulnerabilities.
evidence: Ensures that security patches for all assigned information systems are installed within the timeframe identified by ED policy;

Ensures that actions are taken to respond and comply within specified timelines for any government-wide or ED-wide directed action items related to vulnerability patching; This includes actions directed by the DHS, which issues 'Binding Operational Directives' (BODs), that mandate reporting requirements by the Department for remediating critical vulnerabilities;
Implements proper system backups and patch management processes;

Ensures continuous monitoring of the information system’s security is performed and validates the information system against the System Security Plan (SSP) while managing and controlling any information system updates;
Ensures NIST SP 800-53 (as amended) controls are appropriate to the system based on the FIPS 199 security categorization;
gaps: No explicit definition of patching or remediation SLAs (e.g., patching critical vulnerabilities within a set number of days).
No direct reference to a formalized, risk-based process for prioritizing and remediating vulnerabilities according to severity.
Lack of measured, monitored, or reported metrics for adherence and effectiveness.
No mention of continuous improvement or integration with broader risk management.
recommendations: Explicitly define SLAs for vulnerability remediation by severity (e.g., critical, high, medium, low) and include them in the policy.
Establish and document a formal, risk-based process for triaging, prioritizing, and remediating vulnerabilities.
Implement and monitor metrics for vulnerability remediation (e.g., SLA compliance rates), and assign accountability for meeting these metrics.
Include requirements for periodic review and continuous improvement of vulnerability management processes and their integration with overall risk management.
